title.zh: 卷417 列傳二百四 都兴阿弟：西凌阿 福兴 富明阿 舒保 伊兴额 滕家胜 关保
title.en: Volume 417 Biographies 204: Dou Xinga younger brother: Xi Ling A, Fu Xing, Fu Minga, Shu Bao, Yi Xinge, Teng Jiasheng, Guan Bao
title.raw: 卷417 列傳二百四 都兴阿弟：西凌阿 福兴 富明阿 舒保 伊兴额 滕家胜 关保

sentences.zh: 列傳二百四

translations.literal: Biographies 204
translations.idiomatic: Biography 204

sentences.zh: 都興阿弟西凌阿福興富明阿舒保伊興額滕家勝關保

translations.literal: Du Xing'a, younger brother Xi Ling'a, Fu Xing, Fuming'a, Shubao, Yixing'e, Teng Jiasheng, Guanbao
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a, his younger brother Xi Ling'a, Fu Xing, Fuming'a, Shubao, Yixing'e, Teng Jiasheng, and Guanbao

sentences.zh: 都興阿，字直夫，郭貝爾氏，滿洲正白旗人，內大臣阿那保孫。

translations.literal: Du Xing'a, style name Zhifu, of the Gobulo clan, a Manchu of the Plain White Banner, was grandson of the interior minister Anabao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a, whose style was Zhifu, belonged to the Gobulo clan and served as a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner; he was a grandson of the interior minister Anabao.

sentences.zh: 父博多歡，正黃旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: His father Bodohuan was Mongol commandant-general of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bodohuan held the post of Mongol commandant-general of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 都興阿由廕生授三等侍衛，晉二等。

translations.literal: Through yin-sheng privilege Du Xing'a was appointed a third-class bodyguard and was promoted to second class.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary yin privilege Du Xing'a entered service as a third-class bodyguard and was later promoted to the second class.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，從僧格林沁赴天津剿粵匪，破之於杜家嘴，擢頭等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he followed Sengge Rinchen to Tianjin to suppress the Cantonese bandits, defeated them at Dujiazui, and was promoted to first-class bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng (1853) he followed Sengge Rinchen to Tianjin to fight the Taiping rebels, routed them at Dujiazui, and was promoted to first-class bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 四年，克獨流，追賊阜城，破運河濱賊壘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he captured Duliui, pursued the bandits to Fucheng, and stormed their stockades along the canal bank.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took Duliui, pursued the rebels to Fucheng, and destroyed their fortifications along the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 五年，克連鎮，賊首林鳳祥就擒，加副都統銜、乾清門行走。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he captured Lianzhen; the bandit leader Lin Fengxiang was taken; he was given the nominal rank of vice commandant-general and the privilege of walking within the Gate of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he captured Lianzhen and Lin Fengxiang, the rebel leader, was taken alive; he received the nominal rank of vice commandant-general and permission to walk within the Gate of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 尋授京口副都統。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed vice commandant-general at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon afterward appointed vice commandant-general at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 弟西凌阿督師湖北，都興阿率馬隊往助剿，复德安，從總督官文進規武漢。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xi Ling'a commanded the army in Hubei; Du Xing'a led cavalry to assist in the suppression, recovered De'an, and followed Governor Guan Wen in advancing on Wuhan.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother Xi Ling'a took command in Hubei, Du Xing'a led a cavalry detachment to assist the campaign, recovered De'an, and joined Governor Guan Wen in the advance on Wuhan.

sentences.zh: 時官文軍北岸，趨漢陽，巡撫胡林翼軍南岸，攻武昌。

translations.literal: At that time Guan Wen's army was on the north bank advancing on Hanyang, while Grand Secretary Hu Linyi's army on the south bank attacked Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Wen's force held the north bank and pressed toward Hanyang, while Grand Secretary Hu Linyi attacked Wuchang from the south bank.

sentences.zh: 都興阿率騎兵護水師，敗賊沙口，薄漢陽西門。

translations.literal: Du Xing'a led cavalry to escort the naval force, defeated the bandits at Shakou, and pressed close to Hanyang's west gate.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a led cavalry to cover the fleet, defeated the rebels at Shakou, and closed on the west gate of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊由金鋪山上竄，都興阿揮步隊迎擊，分馬隊抄其後，斬馘甚眾，焚團風鎮屯糧，斬其酋。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the bandits broke out from Jinpufu Hill; Du Xing'a led infantry to meet them, sent cavalry around to their rear, killed and decapitated a great many, burned the grain stored at Tuanfeng Town, and beheaded their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year rebels broke out from Jinpufu Hill; Du Xing'a met them with infantry, sent cavalry around to strike their rear, killed a great many and took many heads, burned the grain depot at Tuanfeng Town, and slew their leader.

sentences.zh: 林翼燔漢陽城外賊艇，賊登岸遁，都興阿以馬隊遮殲之，擢江寧將軍。

translations.literal: Linyi burned the bandit boats outside Hanyang; as the bandits fled ashore Du Xing'a used cavalry to block and annihilate them, and was promoted to General of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi burned the rebel boats outside Hanyang; when the rebels fled ashore Du Xing'a used cavalry to cut them off and destroy them, and was promoted to General of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 襄樊土匪方熾，都興阿馳援襄陽，解其圍。

translations.literal: Local bandits in Xiangyang and Fancheng were raging fiercely; Du Xing'a rushed to relieve Xiangyang and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: With local bandits raging around Xiangyang and Fancheng, Du Xing'a hurried to Xiangyang and raised the siege.

sentences.zh: 進圍武昌，賊糧盡援絕，棄城遁，复武昌、漢陽，乘勝克黃州、興國、大冶、蘄水、蘄州、廣濟、黃梅諸城，賜號霍欽巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Wuchang; the bandits' provisions ran out and reinforcements ceased; they abandoned the city and fled; he recovered Wuchang and Hanyang and, pressing the advantage, captured Huangzhou, Xingguo, Daye, Qishui, Qizhou, Guangji, Huangmei, and other cities, and was granted the epithet Huoqin Batuer.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the siege of Wuchang until the rebels, out of food and cut off from relief, abandoned the city; he recovered Wuchang and Hanyang and, riding the momentum, took Huangzhou, Xingguo, Daye, Qishui, Qizhou, Guangji, Huangmei, and other towns, and was granted the honorific title Huoqin Batuer.

sentences.zh: 大軍進規九江，南路李續賓主之，北路都興阿主之。

translations.literal: The main army advanced on Jiujiang; Li Xubin commanded the southern route and Du Xing'a the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: The main force then moved against Jiujiang, with Li Xubin in charge of the southern wing and Du Xing'a of the northern.

sentences.zh: 七年，賊由太湖竄窺黃梅，都興阿空城誘之，盡殲騎賊千餘，其由獨山鎮來襲者，馬步合擊，擒斬數千。

translations.literal: In the seventh year bandits from Taihu probed toward Huangmei; Du Xing'a emptied the city to lure them and annihilated more than a thousand mounted bandits; those who came to attack from Dushan Town were struck by combined horse and foot forces, and several thousand were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year rebels from Taihu probed Huangmei; Du Xing'a left the city empty as bait and wiped out more than a thousand cavalry; another column coming from Dushan Town was caught by a combined cavalry and infantry attack, and several thousand were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 進攻小池口，令多隆阿等破段窯、楓樹坳、獨山鎮賊巢。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Xiaochikou and ordered Dolonga and others to storm the bandit nests at Duanyao, Fengshu'ao, and Dushan Town.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed the attack on Xiaochikou and ordered Dolonga and others to take the rebel strongholds at Duanyao, Fengshu'ao, and Dushan Town.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成大舉麕至，都興阿令多隆阿出黃梅，鮑超屯孔壟，自督馬步攻渡河橋，平二十餘壘，俘斬數千。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng came in force; Du Xing'a ordered Dolonga out from Huangmei, Bao Chao to hold Konglong, and personally directed horse and foot to attack the river-crossing bridge, leveling more than twenty stockades and capturing or killing several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yucheng arrived with a large force, Du Xing'a sent Dolonga out from Huangmei, posted Bao Chao at Konglong, and personally led cavalry and infantry against the river-crossing bridge, leveling more than twenty fortifications and killing or capturing several thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 會合楊岳斌、李續賓水陸軍攻童司牌，盡平賊壘。

translations.literal: He joined Yang Yuebin's and Li Xubin's combined land and naval forces to attack Tongsipai and leveled all the bandit stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Yang Yuebin and Li Xubin in a combined land-and-water assault on Tongsipai and cleared out every rebel fortification.

sentences.zh: 進克黃蠟山，先後殲賊萬餘，玉成遁走。

translations.literal: He advanced and captured Huanglashan, annihilating more than ten thousand bandits in successive engagements; Yucheng fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Huanglashan, killing more than ten thousand rebels in a series of fights, and Yucheng withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔都興阿幫辦官文軍務。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Du Xing'a to assist in Guan Wen's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Du Xing'a to assist Guan Wen in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 攻小池口，燔其城，遂會克湖口，破賊彭澤，下望江、東流。

translations.literal: He attacked Xiaochikou and burned its city, then joined in capturing Hukou, defeated the bandits at Pengze, and advanced down to Wangjiang and Dongliu.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Xiaochikou and burned the town, then helped take Hukou, routed the rebels at Pengze, and pushed on to Wangjiang and Dongliu.

sentences.zh: 八年，會克九江，被優敘。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he joined in capturing Jiujiang and received special commendation in the records.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took part in the capture of Jiujiang and received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 复黃安、麻城，分軍破賊彌陀鎮、南陽河，复太湖，偕李續賓軍會攻石牌，克之，授荊州將軍。

translations.literal: He recovered Huang'an and Macheng, detached forces to defeat the bandits at Mituo Town and Nanyang River, recovered Taihu, and together with Li Xubin's army jointly attacked Shipai and captured it; he was appointed General of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Huang'an and Macheng, sent detachments to defeat rebels at Mituo Town and the Nanyang River, retook Taihu, and with Li Xubin's army jointly stormed and took Shipai; he was then appointed General of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會水師進規安慶，奪集賢關，薄安慶北門，破賊壘環攻。

translations.literal: Together with the naval force he advanced on Anqing, seized Jixian Pass, pressed close to Anqing's north gate, stormed the bandit stockades, and invested the city.
translations.idiomatic: With the fleet he moved on Anqing, seized Jixian Pass, closed on the north gate, stormed the outer works, and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 而李續賓戰歿三河，桐城、舒城再失，都興阿率軍退保宿松。

translations.literal: But Li Xubin fell in battle at Sanhe; Tongcheng and Shucheng were lost again; Du Xing'a led his army back to hold Susong.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xubin was killed at Sanhe and Tongcheng and Shucheng were lost again, Du Xing'a withdrew his army to Susong.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿偕鮑超大破賊於花涼亭，楚師復振。

translations.literal: Dolonga together with Bao Chao inflicted a great defeat on the bandits at Hualiangting, and the Hunan army revived its strength.
translations.idiomatic: Dolonga and Bao Chao then routed the rebels at Hualiangting, and the Hunan forces regained their momentum.

sentences.zh: 九年，曾國籓奏請於安徽上游北岸添馬步三萬人，以都興阿領其軍，會病足，薦多隆阿自代，詔赴荊州本任。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Zeng Guofan memorialized to add thirty thousand horse and foot on the north bank of the upper Anhui sector, with Du Xing'a to command them; but he fell ill in the foot, recommended Dolonga to replace himself, and was ordered to proceed to his post at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Zeng Guofan asked that thirty thousand cavalry and infantry be added on the north bank of upper Anhui under Du Xing'a's command; Du Xing'a, however, fell ill with a foot ailment, recommended Dolonga to replace him, and was ordered back to his post at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，江南大營潰，上命都興阿帥馬步援江北，而以曾國籓總督兩江。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Jiangnan Grand Camp collapsed; the emperor ordered Du Xing'a to lead horse and foot to relieve the north of the Yangtze, while Zeng Guofan was made governor-general of the Two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Jiangnan Grand Camp collapsed; the emperor ordered Du Xing'a to lead cavalry and infantry to reinforce the north bank of the Yangtze, while Zeng Guofan was appointed governor-general of the Two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 時英法聯軍犯京師，都興阿備北援，馳抵壽州。

translations.literal: At that time the Anglo-French allied armies threatened the capital; Du Xing'a prepared to go north in relief and hurried to Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Anglo-French allied armies threatened Beijing, Du Xing'a prepared to march north in relief and hurried as far as Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 和議成，命赴揚州督辦江北軍務。

translations.literal: After peace was concluded he was ordered to proceed to Yangzhou to supervise military affairs north of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace was concluded he was ordered to Yangzhou to take charge of military affairs north of the river.

sentences.zh: 十一年，令總兵吳全美率師船攻和州江下關，毀​​賊壘，破內江口賊船。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he ordered Brigadier Wu Quanmei to lead war junks to attack Jiangxiaguan below Hezhou on the river, destroy the bandit stockades, and break the bandit boats at the inner river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he ordered Brigadier Wu Quanmei to take the war fleet against Jiangxiaguan below Hezhou, destroy the rebel fortifications, and smash their boats at the inner river mouth.

sentences.zh: 都興阿樂用楚軍，胡林翼分其軍以畀國籓，揚州兵單，留徐州鎮總兵詹啟綸從剿，令提督黃開榜焚三河賊船。

translations.literal: Du Xing'a was fond of using Hunan troops; Hu Linyi divided his army to give to Guofan; Yangzhou's forces were few; he retained Xuzhou garrison Brigadier Zhan Qilun to follow in the suppression and ordered Admiral Huang Kaibang to burn the bandit boats at Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a preferred Hunan troops, but Hu Linyi had detached part of his force for Guofan; with few men at Yangzhou he kept Xuzhou garrison Brigadier Zhan Qilun with him and ordered Admiral Huang Kaibang to burn the rebel boats at Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 賊由儀徵犯揚州，都興阿遣總兵王萬清防湖西，自率三百騎出覘賊，賊眾萬餘，列陣待。

translations.literal: Bandits from Yizheng invaded Yangzhou; Du Xing'a sent Brigadier Wang Wanqing to guard the west of the lake and personally led three hundred cavalry out to reconnoiter the bandits; the bandits numbered more than ten thousand and drew up in battle array to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Yizheng threatened Yangzhou; Du Xing'a posted Brigadier Wang Wanqing on the west shore of the lake and rode out himself with three hundred cavalry to scout the enemy, who numbered more than ten thousand and had formed for battle.

sentences.zh: 都興阿令騎皆下，自席地坐，賊疑有伏，不敢逼，後軍至，奮擊破之。

translations.literal: Du Xing'a ordered all the cavalry to dismount and himself sat on the ground; the bandits suspected an ambush and did not dare press close; when the rear troops arrived he charged fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a had his men dismount and sat on the ground himself; the rebels, suspecting an ambush, held back; when his reinforcements arrived he charged and routed them.

sentences.zh: 賊又糾蘇州、句容悍黨分犯瓜洲、鎮江，都興阿乘其壘未成，令營總杜嘎爾率馬步軍衝擊，自督隊繼之，賊大潰。

translations.literal: The bandits again gathered fierce fighters from Suzhou and Jurong to attack Guazhou and Zhenjiang in separate columns; Du Xing'a, while their stockades were not yet finished, ordered battalion commander Duga'er to lead horse and foot in a charge and personally followed with his column; the bandits collapsed in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then rallied tough bands from Suzhou and Jurong to strike Guazhou and Zhenjiang; before their works were complete Du Xing'a sent Battalion Commander Duga'er forward with cavalry and infantry and followed with his own column, and the rebels broke completely.

sentences.zh: 詹啟綸乘勢踏毀甘泉山賊壘，鎮江圍解。

translations.literal: Zhan Qilun took advantage of the momentum to storm and destroy the bandit stockades on Ganquan Hill, and the siege of Zhenjiang was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Qilun pressed the advantage, overran the rebel camps on Ganquan Hill, and the siege of Zhenjiang was raised.

sentences.zh: 調江寧將軍，仍駐揚州督江北軍，文武悉聽調度。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be General of Jiangning but still remained at Yangzhou directing the army north of the Yangtze; all civil and military officials were to obey his orders.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of General of Jiangning but continued to reside at Yangzhou directing the northern army; all civil and military officers were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 令副都統海全等破後石橋賊營，賊由常州窺鎮江，總兵黃彬統水師擊敗之。

translations.literal: He ordered Vice Commandant-General Hai Quan and others to storm the bandit camp at Hou Shiqiao; bandits from Changzhou probed toward Zhenjiang; Brigadier Huang Bin commanded the naval force and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Vice Commandant-General Hai Quan and others to take the rebel camp at Hou Shiqiao; when rebels from Changzhou probed Zhenjiang, Brigadier Huang Bin with the fleet drove them off.

sentences.zh: 都興阿馳抵天長城下，平其壘卡，賊酋龔長春遁走，沿途截殺殆盡。

translations.literal: Du Xing'a hurried to below the walls of Tianchang, leveled their stockades and checkpoints, the bandit chieftain Gong Changchun fled, and along the route they were intercepted and nearly all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a rushed to Tianchang, destroyed the outworks and checkpoints, and when the rebel leader Gong Changchun fled his men were cut down almost to a man along the way.

sentences.zh: 黃彬等破賊船小河口、太平港，平瓜埠賊巢，尋會江南提督李世忠收降六合、天長二城。

translations.literal: Huang Bin and others broke the bandit boats at Xiaohekou and Taiping Harbor, leveled the bandit nest at Guabu, and soon joined Jiangnan Admiral Li Shizhong in receiving the surrender of the two cities Liuhe and Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Bin destroyed rebel boats at Xiaohekou and Taiping Harbor and cleared the nest at Guabu; Du Xing'a then joined Jiangnan Admiral Li Shizhong in accepting the surrender of Liuhe and Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，江浦、浦口復陷，賊進犯揚州，北營甘泉山，南亙朴樹灣，都興阿親督諸軍連擊，敗走之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Jiangpu and Pukou fell again; bandits advanced to attack Yangzhou, encamping north at Ganquan Hill and stretching south across Pushu Bay; Du Xing'a personally directed the armies in repeated attacks and drove them off in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi (1862) Jiangpu and Pukou fell again; rebels advanced on Yangzhou, camping on Ganquan Hill to the north and along Pushu Bay to the south; Du Xing'a personally led repeated assaults and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 時上游諸軍連克沿江要隘，進薄江寧，都興阿令總兵李起高駛至浦口，襲攻觀音門、燕子磯為聲援，曾國荃大營為援賊所圍，遣副將楊心純率二千五百人赴援，入壕助守，又令黃彬率水師援九洑洲。

translations.literal: At that time the armies upstream captured successive key points along the river and pressed close to Jiangning; Du Xing'a ordered Brigadier Li Qigao to sail to Pukou and make diversionary attacks on Guanyin Gate and Yanziji; Zeng Guoquan's grand camp was surrounded by relief bandits; he sent Deputy Commander Yang Xinchun with twenty-five hundred men to relieve them, enter the trenches to help defend, and also ordered Huang Bin to lead the naval force to relieve Jiufuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While upstream forces were taking the Yangtze strongholds and closing on Jiangning, Du Xing'a sent Brigadier Li Qigao to Pukou to threaten Guanyin Gate and Yanziji as a diversion; when Zeng Guoquan's main camp was encircled by relief rebels he sent Deputy Commander Yang Xinchun with 2,500 men into the trenches to help hold the line and ordered Huang Bin's fleet to support Jiufuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，賊謀入裡下河，都興阿遏之不得逞，別遣副將梁正源會江南軍焚中關、下關賊舟，李起高會收江陰。

translations.literal: In the second year the bandits plotted to enter the Lixia River region; Du Xing'a blocked them so they could not succeed; he separately sent Deputy Commander Liang Zhengyuan to join the Jiangnan army in burning the bandit boats at Zhongguan and Xiaguan; Li Qigao joined in recovering Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year rebels tried to break into the Lixia River lowlands; Du Xing'a stopped them; he also sent Deputy Commander Liang Zhengyuan with Jiangnan forces to burn rebel boats at Zhongguan and Xiaguan, while Li Qigao helped recover Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 三年，江寧合圍，江北無警，而陝、甘回亂益熾，詔都興阿赴綏遠城督防。

translations.literal: In the third year Jiangning was fully invested; the north of the Yangtze was free of alarm; but the Muslim rebellions in Shaanxi and Gansu grew fiercer; an edict ordered Du Xing'a to proceed to Suiyuan City to supervise defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, with Jiangning fully besieged and the north bank quiet, Muslim unrest in Shaanxi and Gansu intensified; Du Xing'a was ordered to Suiyuan to take charge of defense.

sentences.zh: 時甘肅寧夏漢城陷於賊，滿城待援，召都興阿入覲，調西安將軍，督辦甘肅軍務，署陝甘總督。

translations.literal: At that time the Chinese city of Ningxia in Gansu had fallen to the bandits and the Manchu city awaited relief; Du Xing'a was summoned to audience, transferred to be General of Xi'an, placed in charge of Gansu military affairs, and made acting governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: The Chinese quarter of Ningxia had fallen while the banner city still held out; Du Xing'a was recalled to court, made General of Xi'an, put in charge of Gansu operations, and appointed acting governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 江寧克復，論功，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was recovered, in reckoning merit he was granted the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangning was recovered his services were rewarded with the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 六月，都興阿至定邊，奏言回酋馬化隆起靈州金積堡，佔踞城堡，蔓延千里。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Du Xing'a reached Dingbian and memorialized that the Muslim chieftain Ma Hualong had risen at Jinjibao near Lingzhou, seized castles and strongholds, and spread over a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Du Xing'a reached Dingbian and reported that the Muslim leader Ma Hualong had risen at Jinjibao near Lingzhou, seized fortified places, and spread rebellion across a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 定邊距離尚遠，宜進兵花馬池，三路合攻，方期得力。

translations.literal: Dingbian was still far away; it was better to advance troops to Huamachi and attack on three routes together before one could expect results.
translations.idiomatic: Dingbian was still too distant; he argued that the army should advance to Huamachi and strike on three converging routes if the campaign was to succeed.

sentences.zh: 令杜嘎爾等由草地繞石嘴山渡河，攻克薑家村、紅柳溝賊巢，追至寶豐，賊三路出撲，擊敗之，复寶豐，解平羅圍。

translations.literal: He ordered Duga'er and others to cross the river by way of the grasslands around Shizui Hill, captured the bandit nests at Jiangjia Village and Hongliugou, pursued to Baofeng; the bandits came out in three columns to strike; they were defeated; Baofeng was recovered and the siege of Pingluo was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Duga'er by the grassland route around Shizui Hill to cross the river, took the rebel bases at Jiangjia Village and Hongliugou, and pursued to Baofeng; when the rebels sallied in three columns they were beaten, Baofeng was retaken, and the siege of Pingluo was raised.

sentences.zh: 軍進渠公堡，都興阿慮深入無繼，奏調荊州將軍穆圖善會剿。

translations.literal: The army advanced to Qugongbao; Du Xing'a feared that going deep without follow-up support would fail and memorialized to transfer Jingzhou General Mutushan to join the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: As the army pushed to Qugongbao, Du Xing'a worried about overextending without reserves and asked that Jingzhou General Mutushan be sent to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 賊首馬叱吽踞通成堡，突出戰，為杜嘎爾等所敗，退踞清水堡。

translations.literal: The bandit leader Ma Chihong held Tongchengbao, sallied out to fight, was defeated by Duga'er and others, and withdrew to hold Qingshuibao.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Ma Chihong held Tongchengbao, came out to give battle, was beaten by Duga'er, and fell back on Qingshuibao.

sentences.zh: 都興阿移營進逼，絕其糧道，攻克之。

translations.literal: Du Xing'a moved camp forward to press them, cut off their grain route, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a moved his camp closer, cut their supply line, and took the place.

sentences.zh: 進金貴堡、王格莊，去寧夏城二十里，敗西路援賊。

translations.literal: He advanced to Jingui Fort and Wanggezhuang, twenty li from Ningxia City, and defeated the relief bandits from the western route.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Jingui Fort and Wanggezhuang, twenty li from Ningxia, and routed the western relief column.

sentences.zh: 城賊抄官軍後，都興阿督諸軍迎擊，賊大潰。

translations.literal: City bandits struck at the rear of the government army; Du Xing'a directed the armies to meet them and the bandits collapsed in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When city rebels tried to cut the army's rear, Du Xing'a led a counterattack and they broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 四年，列陣城東誘賊出，擊敗之，拔南路賊圩。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he drew up battle lines east of the city to lure the bandits out, defeated them, and took the southern-route bandit stockade villages.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he formed east of the city to draw the rebels out, defeated them, and cleared the southern stockade villages.

sentences.zh: 鹽池、固原竄匪踞安化元城鎮，窺寧條梁糧路，都興阿遣軍分防花馬池、定邊、寧條梁，而靖遠南山賊焚堡據壩修堰，將決渠困官軍，乃移屯城東南。

translations.literal: Bandits breaking out from Yanchi and Guyuan held Yuan Town in Anhua and watched the grain route at Ningtiaoliang; Du Xing'a sent troops to guard separately at Huamachi, Dingbian, and Ningtiaoliang; meanwhile bandits south of the mountains in Jingyuan burned forts, seized dams, repaired weirs, and were about to breach the canal to trap the government army; he therefore moved camp to the southeast of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders from Yanchi and Guyuan held Yuan Town in Anhua and threatened the grain route at Ningtiaoliang; Du Xing'a posted detachments at Huamachi, Dingbian, and Ningtiaoliang, while rebels south of Jingyuan burned forts, seized the dams, and prepared to breach the canal to flood the government camps; he shifted his headquarters to the southeast of the city.

sentences.zh: 賊又踞堤築壘斷水道，並擊退，不得逞。

translations.literal: The bandits again seized the embankment, built stockades, and cut the water route; both attempts were beaten back and they could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels seized the embankment, built works, and tried to cut the water supply, both attempts were repulsed.

sentences.zh: 都興阿親督隊敗賊於金貴堡，分軍屯定邊、花馬池，賊由固原趨平羅、寶豐，截擊於金貴堡，敗之。

translations.literal: Du Xing'a personally directed the column that defeated the bandits at Jingui Fort, detached troops to garrison Dingbian and Huamachi; bandits from Guyuan moved toward Pingluo and Baofeng; they were intercepted at Jingui Fort and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a personally led the force that beat the rebels at Jingui Fort and posted troops at Dingbian and Huamachi; when rebels from Guyuan moved on Pingluo and Baofeng he intercepted them at Jingui Fort and routed them.

sentences.zh: 杜嘎爾擊賊於磴口，斃其酋馬生顏，花馬池、定邊兩路同捷，馘賊首孫義和。

translations.literal: Duga'er attacked the bandits at Dengkou and killed their chieftain Ma Shengyan; the Huamachi and Dingbian routes both won victories on the same day and took the head of the bandit leader Sun Yihe.
translations.idiomatic: Duga'er struck the rebels at Dengkou and killed their leader Ma Shengyan; the Huamachi and Dingbian columns both won on the same day and took the head of Sun Yihe.

sentences.zh: 寧夏賊勢漸蹙，詭辭乞撫，計緩兵，而潛決西河水灌官軍。

translations.literal: The bandit strength at Ningxia gradually tightened; with specious words they begged for pacification to gain time, while secretly breaching the West River to flood the government army.
translations.idiomatic: As rebel pressure at Ningxia eased they pleaded for peace with false promises to buy time while secretly breaching the West River to flood the government camps.

sentences.zh: 都興阿拒其降，益修戰備，進解滿城圍，克城東賊圩，敗之西門橋，分軍擊走大水坑、吳中堡踞賊，斬回酋馬有富，軍威頗振。

translations.literal: Du Xing'a refused their surrender, further strengthened war preparations, advanced to lift the siege of the Manchu city, captured the eastern bandit stockade villages, defeated them at Ximen Bridge, detached forces to drive off the bandits holding Dashuikeng and Wuzhongbao, beheaded the Muslim chieftain Ma Youfu, and military prestige revived considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xing'a rejected their surrender and redoubled preparations; he relieved the banner city, took the eastern stockades, routed them at Ximen Bridge, sent detachments to clear Dashuikeng and Wuzhongbao, beheaded the Muslim leader Ma Youfu, and the army's prestige rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 會奉天馬賊猖獗，調都興阿盛京將軍移剿，而以穆圖善代之。

translations.literal: Just then mounted bandits in Fengtian were raging fiercely; Du Xing'a was transferred to be General of Shengjing to move against them in suppression, and Mutushan replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Mounted bandits then flared up in Fengtian; Du Xing'a was made General of Shengjing to suppress them, and Mutushan took his place in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 穆圖善主撫，寧夏賊尋降，納砲械縛渠以獻。

translations.literal: Mutushan favored pacification; the Ningxia bandits soon surrendered, turned in cannon and weapons, and bound their leaders to present them.
translations.idiomatic: Mutushan favored negotiation; the Ningxia rebels soon surrendered, handed over arms, and bound their leaders for presentation.

sentences.zh: 五年，穆圖善劾都興阿受降入城，仍戮回酋章保立，部下殺掠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Mutushan impeached Du Xing'a for accepting surrender and entering the city yet still executing the Muslim chieftain Zhang Baoli, while his subordinates killed and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Mutushan accused Du Xing'a of accepting surrender and entering the city only to execute the Muslim leader Zhang Baoli while his men looted and killed.

sentences.zh: 詔斥都興阿剿撫無定見，下議褫職，改留任。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Du Xing'a for having no fixed view between suppression and pacification; deliberation was ordered to strip his office, but this was changed to retention in post.
translations.idiomatic: The court rebuked him for wavering between suppression and pacification, debated stripping his rank, but let him remain in office.

sentences.zh: 都興阿至奉天，馬賊漸平，奏定緝捕章程，搜剿餘匪，尋定。

translations.literal: When Du Xing'a reached Fengtian the mounted bandits gradually subsided; he memorialized to fix regulations for pursuit and capture, searched out and suppressed the remaining bandits, and soon they were settled.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengtian the mounted bandits gradually quieted; he drew up pursuit regulations, hunted down the remnants, and soon restored order.

sentences.zh: 七年，西捻張總愚竄畿輔，李鴻章、左宗棠率兵入衛，賊流竄直隸、河南、山東，數月未定。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the western Nian leader Zhang Zongyu broke into the capital region; Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang led troops in to guard the capital; the bandits roamed through Zhili, Henan, and Shandong for several months without being settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the western Nian leader Zhang Zongyu raided the capital region; Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang marched in to defend Beijing while the rebels ranged through Zhili, Henan, and Shandong for months without being crushed.

sentences.zh: 詔召都興阿入京，管理神機營，授欽差大臣，以副都統春壽，提督張曜、宋慶，侍衛陳國瑞四軍隸之，列名在鴻章、宗棠上。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Du Xing'a to the capital to administer the Shenji Camp, granted him the title of Imperial Commissioner, and placed under him the four armies of Vice Commandant-General Chunshou, Admirals Zhang Yao and Song Qing, and Bodyguard Chen Guorui; his name was listed above Hongzhang and Zongtang.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to Beijing to command the Shenji Camp, made Imperial Commissioner, and given four armies under Vice Commandant-General Chunshou and Admirals Zhang Yao, Song Qing, and Bodyguard Chen Guorui; in seniority he ranked above Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang.

sentences.zh: 視師天津，捻匪尋蕩平，仍回本任。

translations.literal: He took command at Tianjin; the Nian bandits were soon swept away and pacified; he then returned to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He took the field at Tianjin; the Nian were soon destroyed, and he returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，卒於官，賜卹，贈太子太保，諡清愨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he died in office; funeral favors were granted; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Qingque.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu (1875) he died in office; the court granted funeral honors, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous name Qingque.

sentences.zh: 奉天士民請與大學士文祥、將軍崇實合建三賢祠，揚州亦請與將軍富明阿合祠。

translations.literal: The gentry and people of Fengtian requested that a Three Worthies Shrine be built jointly with Grand Secretary Wenxiang and General Chongshi; Yangzhou also requested a joint shrine with General Fuming'a.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fengtian asked for a Three Worthies Shrine shared with Grand Secretary Wenxiang and General Chongshi; Yangzhou likewise asked for a joint shrine with General Fuming'a.

sentences.zh: 西凌阿，都興阿弟。

translations.literal: Xi Ling'a was Du Xing'a's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Ling'a was Du Xing'a's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 由拜唐阿授侍衛。

translations.literal: Through the rank of baitang'a he was appointed a bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through the rank of baitang'a and was appointed a bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 道光中，從揚威將軍奕經援浙江，迭晉頭等侍衛，累擢察哈爾都統。

translations.literal: During the Daoguang reign he followed the Yangwei General Yijing to relieve Zhejiang, was repeatedly promoted to first-class bodyguard, and was cumulatively raised to Chahar commandant-general.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang he followed General Yijing to Zhejiang, rose to first-class bodyguard, and was eventually promoted to Chahar commandant-general.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，率黑龍江騎兵從琦善防浦口，因不能阻★匪北竄，褫職留營，責令追賊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he led Heilongjiang cavalry to follow Qishan in defending Pukou; because he could not block the bandits' northward breakout he was stripped of office but kept in camp and ordered to pursue the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he led Heilongjiang cavalry with Qishan to hold Pukou; when he failed to stop the rebels' breakout northward he was dismissed but kept with the army and ordered to pursue them.

sentences.zh: 偕將軍托明阿等馳解開封圍，又敗之汜水。

translations.literal: Together with General Tuoming'a and others he hurried to lift the siege of Kaifeng and again defeated them at Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: With General Tuoming'a and others he relieved Kaifeng and defeated the rebels again at Sishui.

sentences.zh: 賊渡河圍懷慶，援軍會集，西凌阿戰最力，圍解，復原官。

translations.literal: The bandits crossed the river and besieged Huaiqing; relief armies gathered; Xi Ling'a fought most fiercely; the siege was lifted and his original office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels crossed the river and besieged Huaiqing, relief forces gathered and Xi Ling'a fought hardest; the siege was raised and his rank restored.

sentences.zh: 追賊，迭戰王屋、邵原、平陽、洪洞，由山西入直隸，命幫辦勝保軍務。

translations.literal: He pursued the bandits and fought successive battles at Wangwu, Shaoyuan, Pingyang, and Hongtong; from Shanxi he entered Zhili and was ordered to assist in Sheng Bao's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels through Wangwu, Shaoyuan, Pingyang, and Hongtong, entered Zhili from Shanxi, and was ordered to assist Sheng Bao.

sentences.zh: 至靜海，賊踪始定，會軍圍攻。

translations.literal: At Jinghai the bandits' tracks were finally fixed; the combined armies besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinghai the rebels were finally pinned down and the allied armies closed in.

sentences.zh: 四年春，賊走阜城，西凌阿追至後康莊，破之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the bandits fled to Fucheng; Xi Ling'a pursued to Houkangzhuang and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year the rebels fled to Fucheng; Xi Ling'a caught them at Houkangzhuang and routed them.

sentences.zh: 從僧格林沁連破城外賊屯，賊走踞東光、連鎮，攻戰數月，西凌阿常為軍鋒，五年正月，克之，擒賊首林鳳祥，予二等輕車都尉世職，賜號伊精阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Following Sengge Rinchen he repeatedly stormed the bandit camps outside the city; the bandits fled to hold Dongguang and Lianzhen; fighting went on for several months; Xi Ling'a was often the army's spearhead; in the first month of the fifth year it was captured; the bandit leader Lin Fengxiang was taken; he was granted the hereditary office of Second-class Commandant of Light Chariots and the epithet Yijing Batuer.
translations.idiomatic: With Sengge Rinchen he stormed the outer camps repeatedly; the rebels withdrew to Dongguang and Lianzhen and fought for months with Xi Ling'a often in the van; in the first month of the fifth year the place fell and Lin Fengxiang was captured; he received the hereditary rank of Second-class Commandant of Light Chariots and the title Yijing Batuer.

sentences.zh: 又從僧格林沁克馮官屯，俘李開芳，錫封三等男爵，授欽差大臣，督辦湖北軍務。

translations.literal: He again followed Sengge Rinchen in capturing Fengguantun, took Li Kaifang prisoner, was enfeoffed as third-class baron, appointed Imperial Commissioner, and placed in charge of Hubei military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Sengge Rinchen to take Fengguantun and capture Li Kaifang, was ennobled as a third-class baron, made Imperial Commissioner, and put in charge of Hubei operations.

sentences.zh: 初至隨州，戰不利，命其兄都興阿往助，尋褫職，以官文代督師。

translations.literal: When he first reached Suizhou the fighting went badly; his elder brother Du Xing'a was ordered to go assist; shortly he was stripped of office and Guan Wen replaced him in command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: On first reaching Suizhou he met defeat; his brother Du Xing'a was sent to help; he was soon dismissed and Guan Wen took command.

sentences.zh: 從復德安府城，復原官，原駐以固北防。

translations.literal: He followed in recovering De'an prefectural city, had his original office restored, and was originally stationed to secure the northern defense.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in recovering De'an and had his rank restored, remaining posted to hold the northern line.

sentences.zh: 六年，僧格林沁薦之，率馬隊赴河南剿捻匪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Sengge Rinchen recommended him; he led cavalry to Henan to suppress the Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Sengge Rinchen recommended him and he led cavalry to Henan against the Nian.

sentences.zh: 七年，復以屢挫，褫職留任，破張洛行白龍王廟老巢，復之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, again because of repeated defeats, he was stripped of office but kept in post; he stormed Zhang Luoxing's old nest at Bailongwang Temple and had his office restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, after further defeats, he was again dismissed but kept on duty; he destroyed Zhang Luoxing's stronghold at Bailongwang Temple and regained his rank.

sentences.zh: 八年，命駐防山海關。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to garrison Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was posted to garrison Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 十年，授鑲藍旗蒙古都統，從僧格林沁赴山東剿捻匪，尋命幫辦軍務。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Mongol commandant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner, followed Sengge Rinchen to Shandong to suppress the Nian bandits, and was soon ordered to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became Mongol commandant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner, followed Sengge Rinchen to Shandong against the Nian, and was soon ordered to assist in operations.

sentences.zh: 十一年，戰菏澤失利，下部嚴議。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was defeated in battle at Heze; the ministry ordered strict deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was beaten at Heze and the ministry opened a severe inquiry.

sentences.zh: 破賊於東昌，焚賊巢，克七級鎮，進克張秋。

translations.literal: He defeated the bandits at Dongchang, burned their nest, captured Qiji Town, and advanced to capture Zhangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels at Dongchang, burned their base, took Qiji Town, and advanced to Zhangqiu.

sentences.zh: 又破曹州紅川口匪圩，進敗賊於劉家橋、大張寺。

translations.literal: He again stormed the bandit stockade village at Hongchuankou in Caozhou and advanced to defeat the bandits at Liujia Bridge and Dazhang Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He also took the rebel stockade at Hongchuankou in Caozhou and routed them at Liujia Bridge and Dazhang Temple.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，以腿疾回京，授鑲藍旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, because of leg ailment he returned to the capital and was appointed Han commandant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he returned to Beijing with a leg ailment and was appointed Han commandant-general of the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，賜卹，諡勇毅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; funeral favors were granted; his posthumous title was Yongyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died; the court granted funeral honors and the posthumous name Yongyi.

sentences.zh: 福興，穆爾察氏，滿洲正白旗人，都統穆克登布曾孫。

translations.literal: Fu Xing, of the Murca clan, a Manchu of the Plain White Banner, was great-grandson of Commandant-General Mukedengbu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xing, of the Murca clan, served as a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner and was a great-grandson of Commandant-General Mukedengbu.

sentences.zh: 以一品廕生授三等侍衛，出為直隸懷安路都司，累擢督標中軍副將。

translations.literal: Through first-rank yin-sheng privilege he was appointed a third-class bodyguard, went out as commander of Huai'an Route in Zhili, and was cumulatively promoted to deputy commander of the provincial army's central brigade.
translations.idiomatic: Through first-rank yin privilege he became a third-class bodyguard, served as commander of Huai'an Route in Zhili, and rose to deputy commander of the provincial army's central brigade.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，擢廣東高州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to brigadier-general of Gaozhou Garrison in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to brigadier-general of the Gaozhou garrison in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 二年，平羅鏡匪凌十八及鬱林、博白土匪，賜號剛安巴圖魯，擢廣西提督。

translations.literal: In the second year he pacified the Luojing bandit Ling Shiba and the local bandits of Yulin and Bobai, was granted the epithet Gang'an Batuer, and was promoted to provincial admiral of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he suppressed the Luojing bandit Ling Shiba and bandits in Yulin and Bobai, received the title Gang'an Batuer, and was made provincial admiral of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 命援湖南，偕向榮分路追賊湖北，以遷延，奪職留營。

translations.literal: He was ordered to relieve Hunan and, together with Xiang Rong, pursued the bandits in Hubei by separate routes; because of delay he was stripped of office but kept in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to reinforce Hunan, he and Xiang Rong pursued the rebels in Hubei by separate routes; delays cost him his rank, though he remained with the army.

sentences.zh: 三年，從援江寧，屯朝陽門外，屢擊賊，予三品頂戴，充翼長。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the relief of Jiangning, encamped outside Chaoyang Gate, repeatedly attacked the bandits, was given a third-rank official's hat ornament, and served as wing commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined the relief of Nanjing, camped outside Chaoyang Gate, fought repeatedly, received third-rank insignia, and served as wing commander.

sentences.zh: 偕提督鄧紹良破賊東壩，復高淳，會克太平，回軍江寧，迭擊賊於高橋​​門、上方橋、通濟門、雨花台，晉二品頂戴，​​署江寧將軍。

translations.literal: Together with Admiral Deng Shaoliang he defeated the bandits at Dongba, recovered Gaochun, joined in capturing Taiping, returned the army to Jiangning, and repeatedly attacked the bandits at Gaoqiaomen, Shangfang Bridge, Tongji Gate, and Yuhuatai; he was promoted to second-rank hat ornament and made acting General of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: With Admiral Deng Shaoliang he took Dongba, recovered Gaochun, helped capture Taiping, returned to Nanjing, and fought repeatedly at Gaoqiaomen, Shangfang Bridge, Tongji Gate, and Yuhuatai; he rose to second-rank insignia and became acting General of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 母憂，奪情留軍。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was released from mourning obligations to remain with the army.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother's death he was recalled from mourning to stay with the army.

sentences.zh: 六年，授西安將軍，幫辦向榮軍務。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed General of Xi'an and assisted in Xiang Rong's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became General of Xi'an and assisted Xiang Rong.

sentences.zh: 偕張國樑援鎮江，敗賊丁卯橋。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Guoliang he relieved Zhenjiang and defeated the bandits at Dingmao Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Guoliang he relieved Zhenjiang and routed the rebels at Dingmao Bridge.

sentences.zh: 江寧大營潰，向榮退保丹陽，上切責諸將，福興革職留任。

translations.literal: The Jiangning Grand Camp collapsed; Xiang Rong withdrew to defend Danyang; the emperor sternly rebuked the generals; Fu Xing was dismissed from office but kept in post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nanjing Grand Camp collapsed, Xiang Rong fell back on Danyang; the emperor sharply rebuked the generals and stripped Fu Xing of rank while keeping him on duty.

sentences.zh: 榮病卒，命偕張國樑同任防剿。

translations.literal: Rong died of illness; he was ordered to share with Zhang Guoliang the duties of defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Rong died, he and Zhang Guoliang were ordered to share command of defense and suppression.

sentences.zh: 上聞福興與國樑不和，諭怡良察之，遂命福興赴江西會辦軍務。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Fu Xing and Guoliang were not on good terms, instructed Yiliang to investigate, and then ordered Fu Xing to proceed to Jiangxi to join in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Fu Xing and Guoliang were at odds, the court had Yiliang investigate and then sent Fu Xing to Jiangxi to join operations there.

sentences.zh: 七年，复樂平，攻東鄉、金谿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he recovered Leping and attacked Dongxiang and Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he retook Leping and attacked Dongxiang and Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 石達開自安慶竄浮梁、樂平，圍貴溪。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai broke out from Anqing into Fuliang and Leping and besieged Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai broke out from Anqing toward Fuliang and Leping and besieged Guixi.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，福興至弋陽，賊來犯，福興兵少，多為疑兵，賊不敢偪，擊走之，竄浙江，福興進屯衢州東關，賊迭來撲，皆擊退。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year Fu Xing reached Yiyang; bandits came to attack; Fu Xing's troops were few and he used many decoy forces; the bandits did not dare press close; he struck and drove them off; they fled into Zhejiang; Fu Xing advanced to encamp at Quzhou's east pass; bandits came repeatedly to assault and were all beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year Fu Xing reached Yiyang; when rebels attacked his small force he used decoys so they would not close in, then drove them into Zhejiang; he advanced to Quzhou's east pass and repelled every assault.

sentences.zh: 回駐玉山，防賊复竄廣信。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Yushan to guard against the bandits again breaking into Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Yushan to block another rebel thrust into Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 尋又赴衢州，攻東關賊營。

translations.literal: Soon he again went to Quzhou to attack the bandit camp at the east pass.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Quzhou to attack the east-pass rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 福興右腿受傷，尋以傷重乞假，召回京。

translations.literal: Fu Xing was wounded in the right leg; soon because the wound was severe he begged leave and was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded in the right leg, he soon sought leave on account of the injury and was recalled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署鑲紅旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was made acting Han commandant-general of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became acting Han commandant-general of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 同治四年，從尚書文祥會剿奉天馬賊，戰大凌河、北井子，擒斬甚眾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi he followed Minister Wenxiang in jointly suppressing the mounted bandits of Fengtian, fought at Daling River and Beijingzi, and captured or killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tongzhi he joined Minister Wenxiang against Fengtian mounted bandits, fought at Daling River and Beijingzi, and killed or captured a great many.

sentences.zh: 進援吉林，迭破賊於張登、望城岡，署盛京將軍。

translations.literal: He advanced to relieve Jilin, repeatedly defeated the bandits at Zhangdeng and Wangchenggang, and was made acting General of Shengjing.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing into Jilin he repeatedly defeated rebels at Zhangdeng and Wangchenggang and became acting General of Shengjing.

sentences.zh: 五年，擒賊首馬傻仔於黃旗堡，誅之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he captured the bandit leader Ma Shazai at Huangqibao and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he captured the bandit leader Ma Shazai at Huangqibao and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 事平，凱旋，授察哈爾都統，調綏遠城將軍。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he returned in triumph, was appointed Chahar commandant-general, and was transferred to be General of Suiyuan City.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he returned in triumph, became Chahar commandant-general, and was transferred to General of Suiyuan.

sentences.zh: 六年，以舊傷發乞休，光緒四年，卒，賜卹，諡莊愨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because old wounds flared up, he begged to retire; in the fourth year of Guangxu he died; funeral favors were granted; his posthumous title was Zhuangque.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year old wounds forced him to retire; he died in the fourth year of Guangxu; the court granted funeral honors and the posthumous name Zhuangque.

sentences.zh: 富明阿，字治安，袁氏，漢軍正白旗人，明兵部尚書崇煥裔孫。

translations.literal: Fuming'a, style name Zhian, of the Yuan clan, a Han bannerman of the Plain White Banner, was a descendant of Ming Minister of War Yuan Chonghuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fuming'a, whose style was Zhian, was a Yuan-clan Han bannerman of the Plain White Banner and a descendant of the Ming Minister of War Yuan Chonghuan.

sentences.zh: 崇煥裔死，家流寓汝寧，有子文弼，從軍有功，編入寧古塔漢軍。

translations.literal: When Chonghuan's descendant died the family sojourned at Runing; there was a son Wenbi who earned merit in military service and was enrolled in the Ningguta Han banners.
translations.idiomatic: After Chonghuan's line died out the family settled at Runing; a son Wenbi won merit in service and was enrolled in the Ningguta Han banners.

sentences.zh: 五傳至富明阿，以馬甲從征喀什噶爾，授驍騎校，洊升參領。

translations.literal: After five generations Fuming'a came forth; as an armored cavalryman he followed the campaign in Kashgar, was appointed commandant of valiant cavalry, and was repeatedly promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations later came Fuming'a, who served as armored cavalry in the Kashgar campaign, became commandant of valiant cavalry, and rose to company commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，從欽差大臣琦善軍揚州，戰於洞清鋪，受槍傷，裹創奮鬥，斬馘數十，擢協領，特賜玉《角枼》。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he followed Imperial Commissioner Qishan's army at Yangzhou, fought at Dongqingpu, received a gunshot wound, bound his wound and fought fiercely, killed and decapitated several tens, was promoted to deputy company commander, and was specially granted a jade horn cup.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he followed Qishan at Yangzhou, was shot at Dongqingpu, bound his wound and kept fighting, killed dozens, was promoted to deputy company commander, and received a jade horn cup as a special gift.

sentences.zh: 四年，破賊瓜洲，賜花翎，管帶寧古塔兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he defeated the bandits at Guazhou, was granted the peacock feather, and commanded Ningguta troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he defeated rebels at Guazhou, received the peacock feather, and took command of Ningguta troops.

sentences.zh: 五年，戰虹橋，戒所部距賊二十步始發矢，射斃賊酋​​，分兩翼搜伏賊，賊潰走，加副都統銜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he fought at Hong Bridge, ordered his troops not to shoot until within twenty paces of the bandits, shot dead the bandit chieftain, divided into two wings to search out ambushing bandits, the bandits collapsed and fled, and he was given the nominal rank of vice commandant-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year at Hong Bridge he ordered his men to hold fire until twenty paces, killed the rebel leader, swept both flanks for ambushers, routed the enemy, and received the nominal rank of vice commandant-general.

sentences.zh: 六年，署寧古塔副都統，迭敗賊於徐家集、硯台山。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made acting vice commandant-general of Ningguta and repeatedly defeated the bandits at Xujiaji and Yantaishan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, as acting vice commandant-general of Ningguta, he repeatedly defeated rebels at Xujiaji and Yantaishan.

sentences.zh: 攻瓜洲，又率隊及六合練勇攻江浦，敗賊於十里橋，賜號車齊博巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He attacked Guazhou, again led his column together with Liuhe militia to attack Jiangpu, defeated the bandits at Shili Bridge, and was granted the epithet Cheqibo Batuer.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Guazhou, led troops and Liuhe militia against Jiangpu, routed rebels at Shili Bridge, and received the title Cheqibo Batuer.

sentences.zh: 又敗賊於朴樹灣、土橋、五新橋。

translations.literal: He again defeated the bandits at Pushu Bay, Tugiao, and Wuxinqiao.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated them at Pushu Bay, Tugiao, and Wuxinqiao.

sentences.zh: 七年，會攻瓜洲，連敗賊富家井、白廟，以副都統記名。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he joined the attack on Guazhou, repeatedly defeated the bandits at Fujiajing and Baimiao, and was placed on the register for vice commandant-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined the siege of Guazhou, beat rebels at Fujiajing and Baimiao, and was marked for promotion to vice commandant-general.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，克瓜洲，詔以副都統侭先題奏。

translations.literal: That winter Guazhou was captured; an edict allowed him to be nominated first for vice commandant-general.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Guazhou fell, and an edict gave him priority nomination as vice commandant-general.

sentences.zh: 充江北軍翼長，進攻江浦。

translations.literal: He served as wing commander of the army north of the Yangtze and advanced to attack Jiangpu.
translations.idiomatic: He became wing commander of the northern army and advanced on Jiangpu.

sentences.zh: 八年春，迭破援賊，復其城。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year he repeatedly defeated relief bandits and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year he repeatedly defeated relief forces and recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 進屯六合，攻滁州，克來安，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: He advanced to encamp at Liuhe, attacked Chuzhou, captured Lai'an, and was given first-rank hat ornament.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Liuhe, attacked Chuzhou, took Lai'an, and received first-rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 八月，德興阿兵敗浦口，富明阿馳援失利，傷亡幾半。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Dexing'a's army was defeated at Pukou; Fuming'a hurried to relieve them but failed; casualties were nearly half.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, when Dexing'a was beaten at Pukou, Fuming'a's relief force failed and lost nearly half its men.

sentences.zh: 退儀徵，收集散卒，復成軍，扼萬福橋，破賊於運河東，授寧古塔副都統。

translations.literal: He withdrew to Yizheng, gathered scattered soldiers, re-formed the army, held Wanfu Bridge, defeated the bandits east of the canal, and was appointed vice commandant-general of Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to Yizheng, rallied his scattered troops, re-formed the army, held Wanfu Bridge, routed rebels east of the canal, and was appointed vice commandant-general of Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 偕張國樑克揚州、儀徵，又破賊於冶鋪橋。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Guoliang he captured Yangzhou and Yizheng and again defeated the bandits at Yepu Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhang Guoliang he took Yangzhou and Yizheng and again defeated rebels at Yepu Bridge.

sentences.zh: 九年，德興阿以失律罷黜，江北軍不署統帥，命歸和春節制，別選謀勇可當一面者，和春以富明阿薦，詔幫辦和春軍務。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Dexing'a was dismissed for misconduct; the northern army had no appointed commander-in-chief; troops were ordered to return to He Chun's control; another brave and resourceful man fit to hold an independent command was to be chosen; He Chun recommended Fuming'a; an edict ordered him to assist in He Chun's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Dexing'a was dismissed for misconduct and the northern army lacked a commander; troops reverted to He Chun's control until He Chun recommended Fuming'a as a man fit to hold an independent command, and the court ordered him to assist He Chun.

sentences.zh: 時六合、浦口皆未復，富明阿督軍進攻，迭戰百龍廟、李家營及六合城外。

translations.literal: At that time Liuhe and Pukou were still not recovered; Fuming'a directed the army in attack and fought successive battles at Bailong Temple, Lijia Camp, and outside Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: With Liuhe and Pukou still in rebel hands, Fuming'a led repeated attacks at Bailong Temple, Lijia Camp, and outside Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 既而賊數万撲營，分股繞襲後路，遂大挫。

translations.literal: Then tens of thousands of bandits assaulted the camp; separate columns circled to strike the rear route, and there was a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Then tens of thousands of rebels stormed the camp while other columns circled to cut the rear, and the army suffered a major defeat.

sentences.zh: 富明阿身被十二創，詔許開缺回旗醫治，傷已成殘，命以原品休致，食全俸。

translations.literal: Fuming'a received twelve wounds on his body; an edict permitted him to vacate his post and return to his banner for medical treatment; the wounds had left him crippled; he was ordered to retire at his original rank with full salary.
translations.idiomatic: Fuming'a took twelve wounds; the court let him vacate his post and return to his banner for treatment; crippled by his injuries, he retired at full pay on his former rank.

sentences.zh: 十一年，召至京，命訓練京營。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned to the capital and ordered to train the capital garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was called to Beijing to train the capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，授正紅旗漢軍都統，管理神機營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was appointed Han commandant-general of the Plain Red Banner and administered the Shenji Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he became Han commandant-general of the Plain Red Banner and commanded the Shenji Camp.

sentences.zh: 尋命赴揚州幫辦都興阿軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to proceed to Yangzhou to assist in Du Xing'a's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to Yangzhou to assist Du Xing'a.

sentences.zh: 江北里下河十餘縣未被賊擾，鹽場之利如故，偕都興阿疏請運鹽濟餉，軍用得給。

translations.literal: More than ten counties of the Lixia River region north of the Yangtze had not been disturbed by bandits; the profits of the salt fields remained as before; together with Du Xing'a he memorialized to transport salt to supply provisions, and the army's needs were met.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten counties of the Lixia lowlands had escaped the rebels and salt profits continued; he and Du Xing'a memorialized to ship salt for provisions, keeping the army supplied.

sentences.zh: 長江下游南北岸要口四十餘處，排椿駐船，分撥水師扼要駐防，疏陳部署情形，詔特嘉其諳悉地勢。

translations.literal: At more than forty key points on the north and south banks of the lower Yangtze, piles were set and ships stationed; the naval force was divided and posted to hold key points; he memorialized describing the deployment; an edict especially praised his thorough knowledge of the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: At more than forty key points along the lower Yangtze he posted piles and ships and divided the fleet for defense; the court especially praised his grasp of the terrain.

sentences.zh: 賊屢糾捻匪窺伺江北，迭擊走之。

translations.literal: The bandits repeatedly gathered Nian bandits to watch for chances north of the Yangtze; he repeatedly struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels repeatedly sent Nian allies to probe the north bank, and he drove them back each time.

sentences.zh: 分軍渡江助馮子材守鎮江。

translations.literal: He detached troops to cross the river and help Feng Zicai defend Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops across the river to help Feng Zicai hold Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，親率精銳援臨淮，會僧格林沁剿苗沛霖，詔幫辦軍務，令部將詹啟綸、克蒙額會陳國瑞等進攻，連破賊，沛霖伏誅。

translations.literal: That autumn he personally led picked troops to relieve Linhuai, joined Sengge Rinchen in suppressing Miao Peilin, was ordered to assist in military affairs, and directed his subordinates Zhan Qilun, Kemonge, Chen Guorui, and others to advance; they repeatedly defeated the bandits and Peilin was executed in hiding.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he led elite troops to Linhuai, joined Sengge Rinchen against Miao Peilin, was made assistant commander, and through Zhan Qilun, Kemonge, and Chen Guorui won successive victories until Peilin was killed.

sentences.zh: 傷發，請假就醫清淮，疏陳皖北圩練之弊，詔下僧格林沁、曾國籓議加整頓。

translations.literal: His wounds flared up; he begged leave to seek treatment at Qinghuai; he memorialized on the abuses of stockade militia in northern Anhui; an edict was sent down to Sengge Rinchen and Zeng Guofan to discuss strengthening regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When his wounds reopened he took leave for treatment at Qinghuai and memorialized on abuses among northern Anhui stockade militia; the court ordered Sengge Rinchen and Zeng Guofan to tighten regulation.

sentences.zh: 三年春，都興阿赴陝、甘剿回，詔促富明阿回揚州坐鎮，署江寧將軍，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year Du Xing'a went to Shaanxi and Gansu to suppress the Muslims; an edict urged Fuming'a to return to Yangzhou to hold command, made him acting General of Jiangning, and soon gave him the substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year, as Du Xing'a went to Shaanxi and Gansu, Fuming'a was ordered back to Yangzhou, made acting then substantive General of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 遣詹啟綸率兵渡江助剿，克丹陽，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He sent Zhan Qilun to lead troops across the river to assist in suppression, captured Danyang, and was granted the yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhan Qilun across the river, took Danyang, and received the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 江寧克復，予騎都尉世職，仍督所部水陸諸軍留防江北。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was recovered he was granted the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant and still directed his land and naval forces in remaining to guard the north of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: After Nanjing was recovered he received the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant and continued to command his forces guarding the north bank.

sentences.zh: 於是裁撤紅單船，由提督吳全美率回廣東，酌裁陸軍數千。

translations.literal: Thereupon the red-banner foreign ships were disbanded and Admiral Wu Quanmei led them back to Guangdong; several thousand infantry were judiciously reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign red-banner fleet was then disbanded and sent back to Guangdong under Admiral Wu Quanmei, and several thousand infantry were cut.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「江寧駐防，亂後僅存男婦六百餘人，現設官二十七員，兵二百五十八名，稍存營製。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The Jiangning garrison after the rebellion had only a little more than six hundred men and women surviving; at present there are twenty-seven officials and two hundred fifty-eight soldiers, and the camp system is slightly preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "After the rebellion the Nanjing garrison had only about six hundred people left; it now has twenty-seven officers and 258 soldiers and retains something of camp organization.

sentences.zh: 京口駐防，尚存四千餘人，官兵挑補足額，俸餉不能全支，房屋均已焚毀。

translations.literal: The Jingkou garrison still has a little more than four thousand people; officers and soldiers have been selected to fill the quota, but salaries cannot be paid in full and all buildings have been burned.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingkou garrison still has over four thousand people with ranks filled, but pay is incomplete and all buildings are burned.

sentences.zh: 請飭撥餉修蓋房屋，使有依歸。

translations.literal: I request that funds be allocated to repair and rebuild houses so they may have a place to rely on."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that funds be allocated to rebuild housing so they have somewhere to live."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 四年，因腿傷未痊，請開缺，予假赴京醫治，許坐肩輿，至京，仍命管理神機營。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because his leg wound had not healed, he requested to vacate his post; leave was granted to go to the capital for treatment; he was permitted to ride in a sedan chair; on reaching the capital he was still ordered to administer the Shenji Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, with his leg wound unhealed, he asked to vacate his post and was granted leave for treatment in Beijing, permitted a sedan chair, and on arrival was again put in charge of the Shenji Camp.

sentences.zh: 傷病久不愈，詔允回旗。

translations.literal: His wounds and illness long failed to heal; an edict permitted him to return to his banner.
translations.idiomatic: When his wounds and illness persisted, the court let him return to his banner.

sentences.zh: 五年，起授吉林將軍，督剿馬賊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled and appointed General of Jilin to supervise suppression of mounted bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled as General of Jilin to suppress mounted bandits.

sentences.zh: 力疾進搜山險，遣將分捕，數月肅清。

translations.literal: Despite illness he advanced to search the mountain defiles, sent generals to capture separately, and in several months all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Despite illness he pushed into the mountains, sent generals on separate sweeps, and pacified the region within months.

sentences.zh: 招撫金匪，開闢閒田至數万頃。

translations.literal: He pacified gold bandits and opened idle land reaching tens of thousands of mu.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified gold miners and opened tens of thousands of mu of idle land.

sentences.zh: 不及十年，遂開建郡縣焉。

translations.literal: In less than ten years prefectures and counties were established there.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years prefectures and counties were established there.

sentences.zh: 在任四年，復以傷病陳情乞罷，允之，仍在家食全俸。

translations.literal: After four years in office he again pleaded illness and wounds to beg dismissal; this was granted, and he still received full salary at home.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he again pleaded illness and was allowed to retire at home on full pay.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，卒，優恤，諡威勤。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu he died; special funeral favors were granted; his posthumous title was Weiqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Guangxu; the court granted special honors and the posthumous name Weiqin.

sentences.zh: 吉林、揚州請建祠。

translations.literal: Jilin and Yangzhou requested that shrines be built to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jilin and Yangzhou asked for shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 子壽山，官至黑龍江將軍，光緒中，俄羅斯犯邊，殉難；

translations.literal: His son Shoushan rose to be General of Heilongjiang; during Guangxu, when Russia violated the border, he died a martyr's death;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shoushan became General of Heilongjiang and died defending the border when Russia invaded in the Guangxu era;

sentences.zh: 永山，官三等侍衛，亦於鳳皇城拒日本，力戰死事：皆自有傳。

translations.literal: Yongshan, a third-class bodyguard, also at Fengcheng resisted Japan and died fighting strenuously: each has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshan, a third-class bodyguard, likewise died fighting Japan at Fengcheng: each has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 舒保，字輔廷，舒穆魯氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Shubao, style name Futing, of the Shumulu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao, whose style was Futing, belonged to the Shumulu clan and served as a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 由護軍累擢護軍參領。

translations.literal: From guardsman he was repeatedly promoted to guards company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from guardsman to guards company commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，從僧格林沁剿粵匪，攻圍連鎮，賊乘大風出竄，舒保截殲之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he followed Sengge Rinchen to suppress the Cantonese bandits, attacked and besieged Lianzhen; the bandits took advantage of a strong wind to break out; Shubao intercepted and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he followed Sengge Rinchen against the Taiping rebels at Lianzhen; when they broke out on a strong wind he cut them off and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 五年，竄踞馮官屯，引水灌之，功最，賊渠俘獲，加副都統銜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year they fled to hold Fengguantun; water was led in to flood them; his merit was greatest; the bandit leader was captured; he was given the nominal rank of vice commandant-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the rebels held Fengguantun and were flooded out; Shubao's merit was greatest, the leader was captured, and he received the nominal rank of vice commandant-general.

sentences.zh: 荊州將軍綿洵奏調赴湖北，率馬隊破賊德安。

translations.literal: Jingzhou General Mianxun memorialized to transfer him to Hubei; he led cavalry and defeated the bandits at De'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou General Mianxun transferred him to Hubei, where his cavalry defeated rebels at De'an.

sentences.zh: 六年，迭破黃州李先集、團風賊壘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he repeatedly defeated the bandit stockades at Li Xianji in Huangzhou and at Tuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he repeatedly took rebel stockades at Li Xianji in Huangzhou and at Tuanfeng.

sentences.zh: 胡林翼之圍武昌也，官文令舒保率馬隊三百渡江助戰。

translations.literal: When Hu Linyi besieged Wuchang, Guan Wen ordered Shubao to lead three hundred cavalry across the river to assist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: During Hu Linyi's siege of Wuchang, Guan Wen sent Shubao with three hundred cavalry across the river to help.

sentences.zh: 城賊、援賊分八路來犯，舒保以勁騎馳突，賊大奔。

translations.literal: City bandits and relief bandits came to attack in eight routes; Shubao charged with crack cavalry; the bandits fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When city and relief rebels attacked in eight columns, Shubao charged with elite cavalry and they broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 平魯家港賊壘，又敗之沙子嶺、小龜山、雙鳳山。

translations.literal: He pacified the bandit stockade at Lujia Harbor and again defeated them at Shaziling, Xiaoguishan, and Shuangfengshan.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared the stockade at Lujia Harbor and again defeated them at Shaziling, Xiaoguishan, and Shuangfengshan.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，大小二十八戰，胡林翼奏稱舒保馬隊之力特多，賜號倭什洪額巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Within ten days there were twenty-eight battles large and small; Hu Linyi memorialized that Shubao's cavalry strength had been especially great; he was granted the epithet Woshihonge Batuer.
translations.idiomatic: In ten days he fought twenty-eight engagements; Hu Linyi praised his cavalry above all and he received the title Woshihonge Batuer.

sentences.zh: 偕知府唐訓方合剿襄陽土匪，迭敗之黃龍橋、餘山店，解襄陽圍。

translations.literal: Together with Prefect Tang Xunfang he jointly suppressed the local bandits of Xiangyang, repeatedly defeated them at Huanglong Bridge and Yushandian, and lifted the siege of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: With Prefect Tang Xunfang he suppressed Xiangyang bandits, repeatedly beat them at Huanglong Bridge and Yushandian, and raised the siege of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 克樊城、老河口賊巢，復光化、房、竹山三城。

translations.literal: He captured the bandit nests at Fancheng and Laohekou and recovered the three cities of Guanghua, Fang, and Zhushan.
translations.idiomatic: He took rebel nests at Fancheng and Laohekou and recovered Guanghua, Fangxian, and Zhushan.

sentences.zh: 雪夜擒匪首高二張家集，誅之，襄陽平。

translations.literal: On a snowy night he captured the bandit leader Gao Er at Zhangjiaji and executed him; Xiangyang was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On a snowy night he captured the bandit leader Gao Er at Zhangjiaji and executed him, and Xiangyang was pacified.

sentences.zh: 餘匪遁入河南境，陷內鄉，七年，舒保躡至，會豫軍殲之。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits fled into Henan territory and captured Neixiang; in the seventh year Shubao pursued to there and joined Henan troops in annihilating them.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors fled into Henan and took Neixiang; in the seventh year Shubao pursued them and, with Henan forces, destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 八年，授鑲黃旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Han vice commandant-general of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Han vice commandant-general of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 舒保方駐防商城，而賊由六安進犯湖北，陷麻城，急回軍趨黃州。

translations.literal: Shubao was just garrisoning Shangcheng when bandits from Lu'an advanced to invade Hubei and captured Macheng; he hurriedly returned his army toward Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Shubao was at Shangcheng, rebels from Lu'an invaded Hubei and took Macheng; he rushed back toward Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 南勇敗於望天畈，為賊追逼，舒保迎擊，戰一晝夜，賊始退。

translations.literal: Southern militia were defeated at Wangtianfan and pursued by bandits; Shubao met them in attack and fought one day and night before the bandits finally withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When southern militia were beaten at Wangtianfan and pursued, Shubao met the attack and fought for a day and night before the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又偕李續宜破諸蘄水。

translations.literal: He again joined Li Xuyi in defeating the bandits at various places in Qishui.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Li Xuyi in clearing rebel positions around Qishui.

sentences.zh: 時欽差大臣勝保援固始，兵未利，而商城又告警。

translations.literal: At that time Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao was relieving Gushi but the army had not yet gained advantage, while Shangcheng again sounded alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Commissioner Sheng Bao was relieving Gushi without success when Shangcheng was threatened again.

sentences.zh: 勝保嚴檄舒保助剿，胡林翼疏言：「舒保樸訥忠勇，在楚有年，洪山之戰，襄陽之役，蘄、黃之捷，實能為人所難為，從無就易避難之意。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao sent a stern dispatch ordering Shubao to assist in suppression; Hu Linyi memorialized: "Shubao is plainspoken, loyal, and brave; he has been in Chu for years; at the battle of Hongshan, the campaign of Xiangyang, and the victories at Qi and Huang, he has truly done what others find hard to do and has never shown a mind to take the easy and avoid the difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao sternly ordered Shubao to assist; Hu Linyi wrote: "Shubao is plain, loyal, and brave; he has served in Huguang for years; at Hongshan, Xiangyang, and the victories around Qishui and Huangzhou he has done what others could not and never shirked hard duty.

sentences.zh: 今以特簡二品大員，勝保乃嚴札驅迫，加以苛辭。

translations.literal: Now that he has been specially appointed a second-rank high official, Sheng Bao still drives and compels him with stern dispatches and harsh words.
translations.idiomatic: Though specially appointed a second-rank officer, he is driven by Sheng Bao's harsh dispatches and abusive language.

sentences.zh: 師克在和，古有明訓。

translations.literal: Armies conquer through harmony; the ancients had clear instruction on this.
translations.idiomatic: Armies win through harmony; the ancients taught as much.

sentences.zh: 束縛馳驟，必誤戎機。

translations.literal: Binding and hurrying him will surely miss the military opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Binding and hurrying him will surely ruin the campaign.

sentences.zh: 挾權任術，馭不肖之將，或可取快一時，若忠良之士，不煩督率而自奮也。

translations.literal: Wielding power and using stratagems to control unworthy generals may win momentary satisfaction, but loyal and good men need no urging to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Power plays may cow unworthy generals for a moment, but loyal men need no driving to fight hard.

sentences.zh: 臣謂舒保一軍，應審楚、豫各路賊勢，相機進剿，毋庸強歸鄰省節制調遣。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that Shubao's army should examine bandit strength on the various routes of Chu and Yu and advance suppression as opportunity permits, without forcibly placing it under a neighboring province's control and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Shubao's force should watch rebel movements in Huguang and Henan and strike as opportunity allows, not be forced under a neighboring province's command.

sentences.zh: 」上命舒保仍回羅田、麻城勦賊。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shubao still to return to Luotian and Macheng to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Shubao back to Luotian and Macheng to fight rebels.

sentences.zh: 固始圍解，陳玉成復犯湖北，舒保偕續宜破之麻城。

translations.literal: When the siege of Gushi was lifted, Chen Yucheng again invaded Hubei; Shubao together with Xuyi defeated him at Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Gushi was relieved, Chen Yucheng invaded Hubei again; Shubao and Xuyi defeated him at Macheng.

sentences.zh: 李續賓既克九江，會師攻黃安，下之。

translations.literal: After Li Xubin had captured Jiujiang, the armies joined to attack Huang'an and took it.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xubin took Jiujiang, the allied armies attacked and captured Huang'an.

sentences.zh: 既而續賓戰歿三河，楚邊大震，舒保以所部四百騎自武昌東下。

translations.literal: Then Xubin fell in battle at Sanhe; the Chu border was greatly shaken; Shubao with his four hundred cavalry went down from Wuchang to the east.
translations.idiomatic: When Xubin was killed at Sanhe and the Huguang frontier shook, Shubao led his four hundred cavalry east from Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 林翼次黃州，增舒保軍千人，以新補西丹游牧蘄水、上巴河，而令率舊部赴太湖，為多隆阿聲援。

translations.literal: Linyi halted at Huangzhou, increased Shubao's army by one thousand men, used newly recruited Xidan nomads to roam at Qishui and Shangbahe, and ordered him to lead his old troops to Taihu as a supporting force for Dolonga.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi halted at Huangzhou, added a thousand men to Shubao's command, posted newly recruited Xidan cavalry around Qishui and Shangbahe, and ordered his veteran troops to Taihu to support Dolonga.

sentences.zh: 會別賊又陷德安、黃州、孝感諸府縣，將軍都興阿檄調舒保未至，奏劾其觀望，下部議。

translations.literal: Just then other bandits again captured De'an, Huangzhou, Xiaogan, and other prefectures and counties; General Du Xing'a dispatched orders calling Shubao, but he did not arrive; he memorialized impeaching him for hesitating and holding back, and the matter was referred to the Board for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile other rebel columns took De'an, Huangzhou, Xiaogan, and neighboring seats; General Du Xing'a summoned Shubao in vain and memorialized that he was holding back; the matter was sent to the Board for review.
